description: Carnallite -- the Dead Sea salt ecoinvent's Israeli magnesium takes 9.5 kg of per kg of metal -- is filed from water by both ecoinvent and EF 3.1, and the ecoinvent Centre gives it a `Resource use, minerals and metals` factor of 1.0375e-05 that the JRC does not. The number is chlorine's crustal factor weighted by carnallite's chlorine share, from a rule in the v3.12 implementation report (Table 20) that reads a mineral's formula and not its compartment. The same implementation gives chlorine from water nothing, and #137 recorded why: the indicator depletes the crust, and the ocean is not in it. So the list declines carnallite's number, on the record, in `lcia-factor-rulings.json`; the ecoinvent Centre's statement of it stays published as theirs.

expectations.title: Carnallite taken from water carries no `Resource use, minerals and metals` factor of this list's
expectations.comment: Before the ruling this was true by accident -- a factor only one implementation states sits on the proposed queue and is published by nobody until somebody answers -- and after it, on purpose. The ruling is what turns the queue row from `blocking` to `info`, which the measure below claims.

expectations.title: The ecoinvent Centre's 1.04E-05 for carnallite from water is still published under their name
expectations.comment: A decline withholds this list's number and erases nobody's. Quoted as Table 20 of the v3.12 report prints it; the workbook holds 1.037548743806311e-05.

expectations.title: At least one proposed-factor question is answered by a ruling
expectations.comment: Two on the 21 August 2026 build of `20ad511`, both the pool credit's (#139) and both `publish`; this ruling makes three, and is the first `decline` on any queue. Bounded below rather than stated exactly, because the count is the queue's and a fourth answer to some other question should not fail a claim about this one. The count says the ruling was read and applied rather than merely present in the file.
